text: Lesson 13 gave you the owner — the person Accountable for a data domain. This lesson covers who actually does the recurring work the owner is accountable for: the data steward.

DAMA-DMBOK defines a steward as a business leader or subject matter expert accountable for tasks related to data management. Concretely: maintaining the domain's agreed definitions, monitoring quality against the owner's thresholds, answering what-does-this-mean questions from other teams, and escalating anything they can't resolve themselves.

Stewardship isn't one job — DAMA-DMBOK and the field that followed it generally split it into three flavors. The business steward understands what the data means. The technical steward understands how it's structured and stored. The data management steward owns the glossary, the quality rules, and the documentation. One person can hold all three on a small domain; a regulated, high-risk domain often needs a dedicated person for each.

Put the chain together and you get the backbone of this chapter: the owner is Accountable, the steward is Responsible for daily work, and — as the next lesson covers — the custodian handles the technical implementation underneath both of them.
Owner decides, steward maintains, and next lesson adds the two roles that round out the full picture: custodians and consumers. See you there.
